title: XP How to take a screenshot of the full map?

posts.author: NaMosca
posts.body:
I need his for do the parallax
thank you in advance (I didn't find any script)
edit: so I think I'll do this: Since I want to take a screenshot to edit in the image editing program to make parallax in RPG Maker XP, for small maps that fit entirely on the screen I just need to take a screenshot of the screen and crop it in an editing program. For larger maps I'm thinking of it this way: if I find out the size of the map that fits on the screen, I can create several small maps in RPG Maker XP that fit entirely on the screen, take a screenshot of each one of them and put them all together in a single large map in the editing program, then I need to find a way to convert the size of the image that I created in the editing program to the number of tiles used in the height and width (because in RPG Maker XP to create a map you specify the number of tiles for width and height). I think it's just a matter of dividing the height and width of the image size by 32, because if I'm not mistaken an RPG Maker XP tile is 32x32. And then I create a map of that size, and then I assemble it in the editing program, I cut the image into parts to assemble a tileset and apply it to the RPG Maker XP map.

posts.author: Nirriti
posts.body: IDK if you can on XP, but on MZ, you can rightclick the map's name on the map menu to the bottom left. Then theres an option you can choose which is "SCREENSHOT MAP" or something. Try that! If not there... I'm sorry.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
XP doesn't have that function built in, thus the question in the first place XD
At one point, there
was
a script to do that, but I seem to recall going searching for it within the last couple of years and either coming up empty, or couldn't get it working.
Usually if I need to get a screenshot of a map larger than one game screen, I make my player character invisible and just zoom around the map taking a screenshot and pasting it into GIMP; rinse and repeat, carefully lining them up. It wouldn't be ideal for a gigantic map, but it works for most of what I've done.
But before you devote a ton of time to screenshotting and pasting: the point of parallax mapping in later engines, like I think Andar mentioned in another of your threads, was to make up for their much less customizable mapping systems. XP has a really powerful mapping system, and--depending on what it is you're wanting to do with your maps--you may be better served by making your maps in-engine and simply including a variety of "clumped" pieces on your tileset. "Clumping" the pieces lets you get areas of non-gridded detail without having to make your entire map in a different program--you can think of it as "parallax lite." For example:
This is  a rock, a tuft of grass, some pebbles, and some mushrooms layered together in-engine:
This is the same rock, tuft of grass, pebbles, and mushrooms layered together in GIMP:
Again, I don't know what exactly you're hoping to achieve with parallax maps instead of editor maps--but if you want extra detail that doesn't adhere to the grid, making detailed pieces to use in the editor is easy to do and much faster than making your entire map elsewhere!
